mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares blood with other connective tissues?

options.A: Blood has a liquid extracellular matrix called plasma, whereas most other connective tissues have a solid or semi‑solid matrix.
options.B: Blood contains chondrocytes as its main cell type, similar to cartilage.
options.C: Blood fibers are abundant like the collagen fibers found in tendons.
options.D: Blood lacks any cells, unlike other connective tissues.

mcqs.answer: Blood has a liquid extracellular matrix called plasma, whereas most other connective tissues have a solid or semi‑solid matrix.
mcqs.explanation: Blood is classified as a connective tissue because it has cells (red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets) embedded in an extracellular matrix that is fluid (plasma). Most other connective tissues have a solid or semi‑solid matrix (e.g., collagen fibers in tendons). Options B, C, and D are incorrect: blood does not contain chondrocytes, it has very few fibers, and it certainly contains cells.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about bone tissue is NOT correct?

options.A: Bone tissue is a type of dense regular connective tissue that provides support and protection.
options.B: The matrix of bone contains hydroxyapatite crystals which make it rigid.
options.C: Osteocytes are located in lacunae and maintain bone tissue.
options.D: Bone tissue lacks any blood supply and therefore heals slowly.

mcqs.answer: Bone tissue lacks any blood supply and therefore heals slowly.
mcqs.explanation: Bone is a highly vascular connective tissue; its blood vessels bring nutrients and cells needed for growth and repair, which is why fractures can heal. Therefore option D is false. Options A, B, and C correctly describe bone tissue.

mcqs.question: Cartilage is best described as:

options.A: A flexible connective tissue with cells called chondrocytes embedded in a firm matrix.
options.B: A hard tissue composed of osteocytes and hydroxyapatite.
options.C: A liquid tissue consisting of plasma and blood cells.
options.D: A type of epithelial tissue forming protective layers.

mcqs.answer: A flexible connective tissue with cells called chondrocytes embedded in a firm matrix.
mcqs.explanation: Cartilage is a type of connective tissue that is semi‑rigid yet flexible. Its cells are chondrocytes, which reside in lacunae within a matrix rich in collagen and proteoglycans. Options B, C, and D describe bone, blood, and epithelium respectively, not cartilage.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes a characteristic of areolar connective tissue?

options.A: It contains densely packed collagen fibers with little ground substance.
options.B: It has a loose arrangement of fibers and abundant ground substance, allowing it to act as a packing material.
options.C: It is avascular and receives nutrients by diffusion only.
options.D: It is composed mainly of chondrocytes within a calcified matrix.

mcqs.answer: It has a loose arrangement of fibers and abundant ground substance, allowing it to act as a packing material.
mcqs.explanation: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue with loosely arranged collagen and elastic fibers and a lot of ground substance, making it an excellent filler and support tissue. It is vascular (contrary to option C) and does not contain chondrocytes or a calcified matrix (option D). Option A describes dense connective tissue.

mcqs.question: Adipose tissue differs from areolar tissue in that:

options.A: It stores fat droplets in its cells, whereas areolar tissue does not store fat.
options.B: It contains densely packed collagen fibers, while areolar tissue has loosely arranged fibers.
options.C: It is highly vascular, whereas areolar tissue is avascular.
options.D: It functions primarily in support and protection, while areolar tissue functions in energy storage.

mcqs.answer: It stores fat droplets in its cells, whereas areolar tissue does not store fat.
mcqs.explanation: Adipose tissue is specialized for fat storage; its cells (adipocytes) contain large lipid droplets. Areolar tissue lacks such fat droplets and serves mainly as a filler and support. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the structural and functional differences.

mcqs.question: The presence of a fluid matrix (plasma) in blood enables it to:

options.A: Provide a rigid framework for muscle attachment.
options.B: Transport nutrients, gases, and waste products throughout the body.
options.C: Store calcium salts for bone formation.
options.D: Act as a shock absorber in joints.

mcqs.answer: Transport nutrients, gases, and waste products throughout the body.
mcqs.explanation: Because blood’s extracellular matrix is liquid (plasma), it can flow through vessels, carrying dissolved substances such as oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and metabolic wastes. The other options describe functions of other connective tissues (tendons, bone, cartilage).

mcqs.question: Which example best illustrates why blood is classified as a connective tissue?

options.A: Blood cells are derived from mesenchymal stem cells in the bone marrow.
options.B: Blood forms the outer protective layer of the skin.
options.C: Blood conducts electrical impulses in the nervous system.
options.D: Blood secretes hormones directly into the bloodstream.

mcqs.answer: Blood cells are derived from mesenchymal stem cells in the bone marrow.
mcqs.explanation: All connective tissues originate from mesenchyme (embryonic connective tissue). Blood cells (erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets) develop from hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow, a mesenchymal derivative, confirming blood’s status as a connective tissue. Options B, C, and D describe functions not related to tissue classification.

mcqs.question: A 10‑year‑old child fractures his femur. Which property of bone tissue primarily contributes to the bone’s ability to heal and remodel after the fracture?

options.A: The presence of a dense, calcified matrix that does not allow cell migration.
options.B: The vascular nature of bone tissue providing nutrients and cells for repair.
options.C: The lack of any living cells within the bone matrix.
options.D: The high proportion of elastic fibers in bone tissue.

mcqs.answer: The vascular nature of bone tissue providing nutrients and cells for repair.
mcqs.explanation: Bone is richly supplied with blood vessels; this vascularity delivers osteogenic cells, nutrients, and oxygen essential for fracture healing and remodeling. Option A is false because bone matrix, while dense, is permeated by canals. Option C is incorrect because bone contains living cells (osteocytes, osteoblasts, osteoclasts). Option D is incorrect because bone contains very few elastic fibers.
